name: What is a bathroom threshold and why would I remove it?

mainEntity.name: What is a bathroom threshold and why would I remove it?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathroom threshold, also known as a curb or a step-over, is the raised barrier at the entrance of a shower or bathtub. Removing it creates a curbless or walk-in shower design, which offers several benefits. This modification improves accessibility for individuals with mobility challenges, making it easier and safer to enter and exit the shower. It also creates a more seamless, open aesthetic in the bathroom, contributing to a modern and spacious feel. Threshold removal is a common component of universal design or aging-in-place bathroom renovations.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bathroom threshold is the raised barrier at a shower entrance. Removing it improves accessibility and creates a modern, curbless shower design.
